A1.justification: Both PDFs are versions of Efficient Diffusion Models: A Survey. All 42 pages of v1 and 51 pages of v2 support comparison, including equations, figures, tables and references. Neither contains an appendix.

before.justification: v1 reports a literature survey. Performance figures and illustrated methods are attributed to cited studies; its application inventory and framework capability table do not report original empirical outcomes.

after.justification: v2 remains a literature survey. Its additional performance figures are attributed to other works, and it introduces no original experiment, simulation, user study or empirical data analysis.

M1.justification: Neither version proposes its own diffusion algorithm or model. The expanded method coverage and revised taxonomy describe existing research rather than changes to a procedure developed by this work.

E1.justification: Neither version conducts training or evaluation. Added DAVIS and FlintstonesHD entries in Table 1, and additional application domains in Section 3.1.1, expand the literature inventory rather than datasets or tasks evaluated by the survey.

E2.justification: Neither version evaluates baselines against a proposed method. Table 2 changes its framework membership substantially, but remains a descriptive capability comparison rather than a benchmark comparison.

E3.justification: No evaluation protocol is conducted by the survey in either version. The added Pixel-MSE entry in Table 1 and descriptions of cited studies do not establish changes to the paper's experimental settings.

E4.justification: Neither version reports original ablations, robustness tests or empirical case studies. Expanded early-exit and retrieval discussions explain cited methods; the replacement early-exit diagram is illustrative.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seeds, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals or significance tests. The newly discussed DeeDiff uncertainty module is an algorithm component, not statistical uncertainty reporting for results.

E6.justification: v2 adds quantitative literature summaries, including REPA's ImageNet 256 FID of 1.42 with classifier-free guidance, VA-VAE/LightningDiT's FID of 1.35, and ReDi's twofold speedup. It removes the ResShift 15-step statement and adds AYS's 20-versus-30-step claim. These change reported examples, not original experimental results or same-setting performance between versions.

T1.justification: New Section 2.1.4 adds flow-matching definitions, push-forward and marginalization formulas, FM/CFM objectives, and statements of their formal properties in Equations 14–21. Section 3.1.2 adds the optimal-transport path parameterization. Existing score-matching and SDE/ODE mathematics is relocated, while the explicit CAT prediction-consistency guarantee is removed.

C1.justification: The introduction refines the advertised taxonomy by removing applications as a top-level contribution alongside algorithms, systems and frameworks. Applications remain in Section 2.2, and the abstract's central comprehensive-survey claim and the conclusion remain substantively unchanged.

C2.justification: v2 adds training and fine-tuning trade-offs, hardware and caching applicability guidance, and substantive future directions involving autoregressive hybrids, alternatives to classifier-free guidance, and efficient video attention. It also reframes adaptive-prior benefits around training; the new Leapfrog training-acceleration wording conflicts with the retained figure's inference explanation.

D1.justification: v2 documents retained methods more concretely, including ASE's DiT/U-ViT block-skipping schedules and ReDi's trajectory key-value retrieval. Section 5 adds optimization details and source references for tools such as OneDiff and xFormers. The survey's own repository link remains unchanged.

R1.justification: Coverage expands substantially through latent diffusion, REPA, VA-VAE, Restart, DeeDiff, recent distillation and caching methods, optimization libraries, and future-work references. Make-a-Video is removed. Existing works moved between sections, including consistency models and progressive distillation, remain covered.

P1.justification: v2 reorganizes foundational mathematics into background subsections, restructures efficient training into latent space, loss formulation and training tricks, and moves distillation from compression to sampling. It extensively rewrites retrieval and training explanations, replaces the framework narrative, and adds a Future Work section.

P2.justification: Figure 1 and several category-summary diagrams are substantially revised. Figure 18 replaces the CAT schematic with an ASE schedule illustration. Table 2 is rebuilt with different framework rows, revised capability definitions, colored support symbols and no fine-tuning column. Numerous retained figures are relocated.

improvement.justification: The expanded formal background, latent-diffusion coverage, optimization-focused framework table and concrete future directions make v2 more useful as a technical survey. Accuracy issues limit the gain: Section 3.3.2's claimed 40% AYS reduction does not match its 20-versus-30-step example, and Section 3.3.4 attributes MLPCM to Wu et al. although the bibliography identifies Du et al. These weaknesses temper the benefits of the broader, better-organized coverage.
